text: The Dexter, Prabakaran and Gunawardena (2019) reinvestigation of Stentor avoidance behavior with modern video tracking mainly concluded what about Jennings' hierarchy?
choices: It fully refuted Jennings, showing Stentor has only a single fixed reflex
It proved the sequence is a rigid, deterministic escalation identical in every cell and trial
It showed Stentor exhibits the hierarchy only after explicit training
It confirmed the core behaviors but found the ordering less rigid, better described as a repertoire of responses with shifting probabilities
explanation: The 2019 study confirmed that Stentor performs bending, ciliary reversal, contraction, and detachment, supporting Jennings' core observation, but found the order variable across and within cells, i.e. a probabilistic repertoire rather than a strict deterministic escalation. It did not refute the behaviors (choice 0), prove rigid determinism (choice 1), or show the hierarchy requires training (choice 2).
